title: Coordinate fundamental form, closed Kähler metric, and Wirtinger derivatives
statement: Use the usual fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq0$, let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary modeled on $E=\mathbf C^n$, and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite Hermitian tangent metric [def-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-data]. For a holomorphic chart $e:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V\subset E$, write $T_e(z)$ for the derivative of the transition from $e$ to the preferred tangent chart at $e^{-1}(z)$. Define the first-linear coordinate pairing $h_e(z;v,w)=\langle T_e(z)w,T_e(z)v\rangle_{h,e^{-1}(z)}$, reversing the arguments of the existing conjugate-first pairing. Put $H^e_{j\bar k}(z)=h_e(z;\partial_{x_j},\partial_{x_k})$ and $\omega_e(z;v,w)=\operatorname{Re}h_e(z;iv,w)$, where $\partial_{x_j}$ is the vector with entry $1$ at $j$ and zero elsewhere, and $\partial_{y_j}=i\partial_{x_j}$. The metric is Kähler when, in every compatible holomorphic chart and at every $z\in V$, for all constant real tangent vectors $u,v,w\in E$, $D_{\mathbf R}(\omega_e(-;v,w))_z(u)+D_{\mathbf R}(\omega_e(-;w,u))_z(v)+D_{\mathbf R}(\omega_e(-;u,v))_z(w)=0$; this is the coordinate definition of $d\omega=0$. For a smooth complex-valued coefficient $f$ on an open $V\subset E$, define $\partial_{z_l}f=\tfrac12(D_{\mathbf R}f(\partial_{x_l})-iD_{\mathbf R}f(\partial_{y_l}))$ and $\partial_{\bar z_l}f=\tfrac12(D_{\mathbf R}f(\partial_{x_l})+iD_{\mathbf R}f(\partial_{y_l}))$, using derivatives within $V$. Compatible holomorphic charts mean the maximal atlas of the complex manifold structure.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §2.1 Theorem 2.1 and §3.3 Definition 3.18, printed p.7 / PDF page 7; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Real cyclic exterior differentiation is expanded explicitly.
